 Advancing the World’s Technology Together 

 Our technology solutions power the tools you use every day--including smartphones, electric vehicles, hyperscale data centers, IoT devices, and so much more. Here, you’ll have an opportunity to be part of a global leader whose innovative designs are pushing the boundaries of what’s possible and powering the future. 

 We believe innovation and growth are driven by an inclusive culture and a diverse workforce. We’re dedicated to empowering people to be their true selves. Together, we’re building a better tomorrow for our employees, customers, partners, and communities.

 What You’ll Learn 

• Project Overview: Physical memory is a bottleneck for AI systems; power and heat decide how fast AI models can run. Our lab is building a simulator tool to aid memory architecture and packaging teams in their work, allowing them to visualize how their designs impact power consumption and heat generation quickly without needing a physical prototype and hours of computation. As a software intern, you will gain an understanding of the entire data pipeline as you develop this tool, improving its features or user experience. 

• Skills You’ll Learn:

• Simulation Infrastructure 

• User Interface Development 

• Power & Thermal Engine Development 

 What You’ll Do 

 Samsung’s Power & Thermal Lab is seeking a software engineering intern to contribute in the development of our power and thermal simulation tool. 

 We are a small, fast ‑ moving team where direct ownership and minimal busywork empower every member to tackle the same real‑world problems. Working with authentic data, real partners, and production‑grade results, our contributions flow straight into platforms used across the company.

 As an intern, you will support research and product teams across multiple projects, including providing end ‑ to ‑ end simulation , regression testing , and data ‑ pipeline management . You will work on real projects with tangible results , receive mentorship, and help shape the scope of work in a collaborative environment where hardware, software, and thermal experts work side‑by‑side on next‑generation AI memory technologies.

 Location: Daily onsite presence at our San Jose headquarters in alignment with our Flexible Work policy 

 Reports to: SVP, R&D (Power & Thermal Lab) 

• Build automation pipelines for simulation runs, regression testing, and result tracking. 

• Implement and optimize a trace‑driven power‑thermal simulation engines. 

• Generate transient power maps, perform spatiotemporal hotspot analysis, and interface with reduced‑order/CFD‑calibrated thermal solvers. 

• Develop high-fidelity, advanced RTL- SystemC-, and C-based power macromodels for AI memory component IPs using analytical modeling, LUT, FSM, NN, and their hybrid. 

• Extract activity-, value-, and state-dependent power features from C/SystemC/RTL simulations. 

• Define power-relevant functional states (transaction/state-based abstraction). 

• Calibrate models using synthesis‑assisted anchors and validate against RTL/gate‑level and silicon data. 

• Integrate IP‑level power macromodels into system‑level simulations. 

• Manage time‑indexed simulation flow across power and thermal domains. 

• Complete other responsibilities as assigned. 
 
 What You Bring 

• Pursuing Masters or PhD in Computer Science, Electrical and Computer Engineering, or related major. 

• Must have at least 1 academic quarter/semester remaining 

• C++, scripting workflows in Python or Bash, SystemC and/or transaction-level modeling. 

• Systems‑level software‑engineering skills. 

• RTL design, synthesis and analysis research and/or experience (Verilog/SystemVerilog/SystemC), preferred 

• Experience with large scale simulation or EDA/CFD adjacent tooling environments, preferred 

• Familiarity with discrete event or time stepped simulation architecture, preferred 

• Experience with GPU, computer architecture, AI memory, memory controllers, PHYs, or high-speed I/O, preferred 

• You’re inclusive, adapting your style to the situation and diverse global norms of our people. 

• You’re an avid learner, you approach challenges with curiosity and resilience, seeking data to help build understanding. 

• You’re collaborative, building relationships, humbly offering support and openly welcoming approaches. 

• Innovative and creative, you proactively explore new ideas and adapt quickly to change. 
 What We Offer
 The pay range below is for all roles at this level across all US locations and functions. Pay within this range varies by work location and may also depend on job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. 

 This is in addition to our diverse package of benefits centered around the wellbeing of our employees and their loved ones. In addition to the usual Medical/Dental/Vision, our inclusive rewards plan empowers our people to care for their whole selves. An investment in your future is an investment in ours. 

 Relocation Support Live 50+ miles away from your new office? No worries! We'll provide a stipend to help support your move. 
Housing Stipend Signing a lease on a new place for your summer internship? We'll help you pay your way with a monthly stipend. 
Give Back With a charitable giving match and frequent opportunities to get involved, we take an active role in supporting the community. 
Prioritize Emotional Wellness With on-demand apps and paid therapy sessions, you’ll have support no matter where you are. 
Stay Fit Eating well and being active are important parts of a healthy life. Our onsite Café and gym, plus virtual classes, make it easier. 
Embrace Flexibility Benefits are best when you have the space to use them. That’s why we facilitate a flexible environment so you can find the right balance for you. 

 Hourly Base Pay Rate
 $28 — $68 USD 

 Equal Opportunity Employment Policy  

 Samsung Semiconductor takes pride in being an equal opportunity workplace dedicated to fostering an environment where all individuals feel valued and empowered to excel, regardless of race, religion, color, age, disability, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, ancestry, genetic information, marital status, national origin, political affiliation, or veteran status.

 When selecting team members, we prioritize talent and qualities such as humility, kindness, and dedication. We extend comprehensive accommodations throughout our recruiting processes for candidates with disabilities, long-term conditions, neurodivergent individuals, or those requiring pregnancy-related support. All candidates scheduled for an interview will receive guidance on requesting accommodations.

 Our Commitment to Innovation and Fairness 

 At Samsung Semiconductor, we use Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools in the recruitment process to enhance efficiency. However, AI is used as a support tool, not a final decision-maker. All hiring decisions are made by our human recruiting team and hiring managers to ensure every candidate is evaluated fairly and holistically.

 Recruiting Agency Policy 

 We do not accept unsolicited resumes. Only authorized recruitment agencies that have a current and valid agreement with Samsung Semiconductor, Inc. are permitted to submit resumes for any job openings.

 Applicant AI Use Policy  

 At Samsung Semiconductor, we support innovation and technology. However, to ensure a fair and authentic assessment, we ask that candidates rely on their own knowledge and skills throughout the process. AI tools may be used for basic preparation, grammar, and research, but should not be used to generate or assist with submitted content or live interview responses. If we determine that AI is being used outside these guidelines, we reserve the right to pause or end the interview, and your candidacy may be disqualified.

 Trade Secret Notice 

 By submitting an application, you agree not to disclose to Samsung—or encourage Samsung to use—any confidential or proprietary information (including trade secrets) belonging to a current or former employer or other entity.

• Project Overview: Every new generation of AI accelerator pushes more power through stacked memory, and temperature is now one of the limits on how fast and how dense HBM can be. Our lab builds compact thermal models that turn workload-driven power maps of a 3D-stacked HBM into transient temperature maps in minutes rather than the hours a full CFD run takes, while staying close to CFD accuracy. As an intern you will own one piece of this platform end to end: from the physics and the CFD reference to a validated model that architecture, power, and package teams use to make design decisions. 

• Skills You’ll Learn:

• Heat conduction in 3D-stacked die: TSV arrays, micro-bumps, underfill, and anisotropic effective properties 

• Compact and reduced-order thermal modeling 

• CFD modeling and validation with Simcenter Flotherm 

• Scientific computing at scale: sparse solvers, preconditioning, and fast Python/MATLAB code 

• Power-thermal co-simulation and thermal-aware design of AI memory systems 

 What You’ll Do 

 Samsung’s Power & Thermal Lab is seeking a thermal engineering intern to help build and calibrate models of HBM stacks and package.

 We are a small, fast ‑ moving team where direct ownership and minimal busywork empower every member to tackle the same real‑world problems. Working with authentic data, real partners, and production‑grade results, our contributions flow straight into platforms used across the company.

 As an intern, the models you build feed design discussions for future HBM products. You will work on real projects with tangible results , receive mentorship, and help shape the scope of work in a collaborative environment where hardware, software, and thermal experts work side‑by‑side on next‑generation AI memory technologies.

 Location: Daily onsite presence at our San Jose headquarters in alignment with our Flexible Work policy 

 Reports to: SVP, R&D (Power & Thermal Lab) 

• Build and calibrate CFD models (Simcenter Flotherm) of HBM stacks and packages under realistic cooling conditions, and use them as the reference for fast models. 

• Extend our compact thermal model to new stack heights, die configurations, and base-die power, and quantify its accuracy against CFD in both steady state and transient. 

• Develop homogenization methods that replace fine features (TSV arrays, micro-bump layers, underfill) with effective properties, and establish where they hold and where they break. 

• Speed up thermal solvers by orders of magnitude through model-order reduction, sparse linear algebra and preconditioning, GPU acceleration, or machine-learning surrogates. 

• Run transient simulations driven by real AI workload traces, locate spatiotemporal hotspots, and explore thermal-aware policies such as throttling, refresh control, and power-map scheduling. 

• Evaluate advanced cooling and thermal-interface options (cold plates, two-phase cooling, TIMs, backside cooling) and translate them into boundary conditions and design guidance for HBM. 

• Couple the thermal model with the lab's trace-driven power simulation engine so that power maps and temperature maps evolve together in time. 

• Document methods and results clearly and present them to engineers and lab leadership. 

• Complete other responsibilities as assigned. 
 
 What You Bring 

• Pursuing a PhD (preferred) or Master's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Materials Science, Electrical Engineering, Applied Physics, or a related field. 

• Must have at least 1 academic quarter/semester remaining 

• Strong foundation in heat transfer, especially transient conduction in multi-layer solids and thermal contact resistance. 

• Hands-on experience with numerical methods (finite-volume, finite-element, or finite-difference) and scientific programming in Python and/or MATLAB. 

• Ability to judge simulation results critically (mesh convergence, boundary conditions, energy balance) and to explain discrepancies between models. 

• Experience with Simcenter Flotherm, Ansys Icepak/Fluent, or COMSOL, preferred 

• Experience with compact or reduced-order thermal models, model-order reduction, or ML surrogates for physical simulation, preferred 

• Background in electronics packaging, 3D-IC / chiplet thermal management, or advanced cooling, preferred 

• Familiarity with HPC, sparse linear solvers, or GPU programming, preferred
